rules.label: Fiscale
rules.legalRef: Code des Procedures Fiscales (CPF), art. 64 (modifie par la loi de finances 2025, art. 99) ; Code de commerce, art. 12
rules.notes: CPF art. 64 (as last amended by loi n. 24-08 du 24 novembre 2024 portant loi de finances pour 2025, art. 99, JO n. 84 du 26 decembre 2024), read directly and quoted verbatim by the issue #558 research pass (RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md, section 6): "[...] les documents comptables ainsi que les pieces justificatives, notamment les factures d'achats [...] doivent etre conserves pendant le delai de dix (10) ans prevu par l'article 12 du code du commerce, a compter [...] pour les pieces justificatives, de la date a laquelle elles ont ete etablies." 'La date a laquelle elles ont ete etablies' (the date they were drawn up) is exactly this schema's own `origin: "issueDate"`: the document's own exact issue date, unrounded, never the end of a calendar year (unlike Portugal's own CIVA art. 52 wording, which this same schema reads as `issueDateYearEnd`). Code de commerce art. 12 (texte d'origine, ordonnance n. 75-59 du 26 septembre 1975, JO n. 101 du 19 decembre 1975, re-read to confirm it is still the operative cross-reference in 2024): "Les livres et documents [...] doivent etre conserves pendant dix ans." CPF art. 39 sets a SEPARATE four-year tax-assessment reopening window (a different question: how long the administration can audit, not how long a document must be kept) and does not reduce this ten-year floor. No '13 bis' article exists in this part of the Code de commerce (a lead the research pass specifically checked and ruled out): a '13 bis' does exist, but in the CIDTA, on an unrelated IRG exemption.

notes: Algeria (DZ), issue #558, transcribed 2026-09-30 from RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md (section 6). A single, well-sourced obligation: ten years from the document's own issue date. One of the most solidly settled points of this research pass: the schema's closed `origin` vocabulary expresses the Algerian text's own wording exactly, with no interpretive gap.
